lines.text: The last tram of the night rattles up to the stop. Pip sits down with glue on both hands and one sleeve.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: [I put up posters. On walls. In the dark. Past the police. I am going to sleep for a week.]

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: [Ruby will be pleased. Ruby might even smile. It's hard to tell with Ruby.]
Through the tram window, the Squad van glows under its lamp. The new paint shines like a wink.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: [The van's still spotless. Probably for the best. Probably.]

lines.speaker: hush
lines.text: All units. Unauthorized posters on Market Row. 'Concert, Saturday, you know where.' I do not know where.

lines.speaker: mute
lines.text: Sergeant, the van has been decorated. It says TURN IT UP. In very large letters.

lines.speaker: mute
lines.text: Sergeant, the van is fine. Someone did hum at me on the way past. I've logged it.

lines.speaker: hush
lines.text: Calm, Mute. Measured. Drone and Partners want the walls clean before the offices open.

lines.speaker: hush
lines.text: Find out who printed these. Then find out where they play.
The tram pulls away. For the first time since the Silence Act, Pip is not thinking about getting caught. Pip is thinking about Ruby.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: [I have to warn her. First thing tomorrow. Unless tomorrow is already too late.]
Behind the tram, the posters glow on the gray walls: small squares of color in a city told to keep quiet.
